convoLines.text: "Please — whatever this is, it's getting worse — I'm feverish, a cut gone hot and angry. Will you help me?"
"Rest won't touch this. The heat's climbing and my head's full of cotton. Someone who knows what they're doing — please."
Stand beside them first — same side of the Haven door — then help.
"It's nothing, really. What were you saying?"
"Joseph always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Right. Action time. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Never mind the pantry run — we got it handled. Thanks anyway. I hate to ask this, but I can't shake it. I'm feverish, a cut gone hot and angry. Will you help me?"
"The cut's gone hot and it's spreading — I can feel it moving. Clean it out, wrap it tight, please. Before it turns."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Never mind. You had something to say?"
"Since Joseph died... I keep expecting to see Joseph at the fire. Stupid."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
"All right —" Greta starts to stand, then sinks back down. "Maybe not today. The fire's got me. Tomorrow, when it lets me go — same walk?"
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Rosa grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Greta is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"I rinse the cup twice. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"What's the kindest thing someone's done for you out here?"
"That's the good stuff. Quiet generosity. It's holding this whole thing together."
"Well, Someone saved me the last of the stew once. Didn't say anything, just put the bowl down and walked off. I think about that bowl more than I think about the monsters."
"It never repeats itself exactly. Every message is slightly different. That means it's generating, not reciting. It's thinking in real time."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on the big questions."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Greta nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
You show them Jerusalem Artichoke — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
Sanne: "Can I ask you something? ... I want us to stick together. Properly. Watch each other's backs."
"Stick together, then." They look steadier already.
"About the pantry run — still need hands. Are you in?"
"About the pantry run — I still haven't found anyone. Any chance?"
"Another day like today and we're choosing who eats. Nobody's worked the creek bend, past the treeline in days. We'll fill packs before dark."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"Forget it — go on, I'm listening."
"Joseph killed the things that come at night. I did too. That's a small club, and it's smaller now."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"And... scene. Good talk."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Got a read on anyone here yet? Who should I be watching?"
"I think — Same. But keep your eyes open — some people here are performing, not surviving."
"Watch the quiet ones. Not the loud — the loud tell you everything. The quiet are either thinking or planning, and you can't tell which until it matters."
"Still on your read on people here."
"I don't know you well enough for that. Ask me again when we've survived something together."
"Look, forget it. You wanted something?"
"Joseph is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Alright — carefully, now. Both of us."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Take care out there."
"Can we talk?" Rosa sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
Rosa has an edge today — something curdled.
"Never mind the sickness I'm fighting — we got it handled. Thanks anyway."
"That can wait — it isn't going anywhere. What's on your mind?"
"Last time things were different. They always are." "We both stood at the treeline. Greta held it. I keep replaying my part, looking for the step I missed."
Something eases in their shoulders. They're really talking to you now.
"The fire feels smaller without Greta. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Lucas nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Jerusalem Artichoke — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Every laugh out there feels wrong today. Then I feel wrong for thinking it."
"You're kind. Don't let this place change that."
"Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "The sickness took Greta. I keep washing my hands like it'll bring them back. Stupid."
Something in them stays shut, for now.
"Nobody says Greta's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Rosa nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"My part? I remember them. Someone has to do it properly."
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Jerusalem Artichoke — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I tell you something? I don't actually know how to swim and I'm terrified someone will find out."
"Practical view: Thank you. ...I needed someone to know, and I needed it to stop there."
"Me? Okay." "Listen. I need you to hear this before you go back out there."
"You've seen what's out there. I'm just saying — the treeline at dusk. Don't."
"Thank you. I needed to hear you say it."
"I keep thinking about that The Ugly Beast. It knows this ground now. Keep your eyes up past the treeline."
"It's nothing, really. What were you saying?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "I know you and Jovan were close. I'm sorry."
"Alright, duty calls. This was a good pause."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
"I asked Jovan about the pantry run — Jovan's gone. Still need hands. Are you in?"
"I still need help with the pantry run."
Accept the forage request first. Meet at Haven at dawn on the following day.
"Look, forget it. You wanted something?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Since Jovan died... I keep expecting to see Jovan at the fire. Stupid."
The moment passes without landing. Not yet.

"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Anyway." A small smile.
"what's been happening — that's still where we are."
You show them Physic Nut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Well. My social battery is officially dead."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Teach me something. Anything you know that I don't. Let's move."
"All right. Show me when we work together."
"I'd like to learn something I can use today. Show me while you work, when you have a moment. Trust me. Mostly."
"Still on teaching them something. What's the worst that happens."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Good question." "Jovan is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Sanne nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"I check the treeline every hour. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
You show them Jerusalem Artichoke — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can we talk?" James shifts their weight. "I need something to do. Anything. Please."
James seems lighter — something good landed recently.
"Honestly? I'm alright right now. Just good to talk."
"It keeps getting worse. I can't haul or hunt with it like this — and if it festers, I'm done for. Please, clean it out and bind it tight."
You spend time tending them. This was care, not a promise of a cure.
"Still on that water haul."
Something eases in their shoulders. They're really talking to you now.
"It's nothing, really. What were you saying?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "I dreamed Henry was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."

"I'm picking up Henry's share of the work. Someone should, and it might as well be me."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Hey — I found some Physic Nut today. You were right, it was right where you said."
"Never mind the pantry run — we got it handled. Thanks anyway. We're down to 0 liters of clean water. I need someone to haul water with me at first light. Two of us, half the trips. Will you come?"
"0 liters. That's today's drinking water, and then we're boiling creek water and hoping. We walk together and each carry two liters back. Creek water still needs boiling."
Accept the creek request first. Meet at Haven at dawn on the following day.

echoSample: d34: "Joseph always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
d34: "Since Joseph died... I keep expecting to see Joseph at the fire. Stupid."
d34: "Joseph killed the things that come at night. I did too. That's a small club, and it's smaller now."
d36: "Joseph is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."

halfRationLines: d49: 💧 The cistern won't cover today — the hall's call, no vote needed: half rations until the water runs come back.
d64: "The bins are echoing. We vote half rations — three days, everyone, no exceptions — or the hunters go out hungry and bring back more than hunger."
